headline: DPM METALS DRILLS 716m AT 3.30 g/t AuEq INCLUDING 138m AT 5.71 g/t — BREVENE PORPHYRY SOUTH OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS, ADJACENT TO CHELOPECH
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX/ASX: DPM) released delineation results from Brevene Porphyry South in Bulgaria: 716.60m at 3.30 g/t AuEq from 1,357m depth, including 138.60m at 5.71 g/t AuEq, with a second hole extending 341m at 2.49 g/t AuEq. The potassic alteration envelope exceeds 500m × 500m and 1,000m vertically, contiguous with the operating Chelopech mine concession, and the system remains open in all directions.

headline: SILVER SURGES TO $67.18 ON MONDAY AS OIL DROPS — GOLD POSTS FIRST WEEKLY GAIN IN FOUR WEEKS AT $4,368
snippet: Silver jumped to $67.18/oz Monday morning, up $1.97 (+3.02%), extending last week's Fed-hike reversal, while gold added $26 to $4,368 for its first weekly gain in four weeks. Falling oil prices are easing real-yield pressure and renewing a fiscal-anxiety bid for hard assets as markets price 60% odds of a second hike next month.

headline: VanEck GOLD SWOT: CHINA IMPORTED 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — PHYSICAL DEMAND DIVERGING FROM PAPER PRICE
snippet: VanEck's Monday Gold SWOT highlights China importing over 790 tonnes of silver in the first months of 2026 as a leading demand-strength indicator, while palladium and precious metals moved higher last week on weaker US jobs data. The physical silver demand picture continues to diverge sharply from the paper market, reinforcing the structural deficit narrative.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE TAKES 14.9% STAKE IN SCOUT DISCOVERIES — $25M PLACEMENT UNLOCKS 70% EARN-IN ON IDAHO GOLD PROJECTS
snippet: Scout Discoveries (TSX-V) closed a $25M private placement: Agnico Eagle Mines invested $14.8M for a 14.9% fully diluted stake at $1.50/share, while Electrum Group raised its ownership to 30% with a $10.2M top-up. Agnico Eagle gains earn-in rights to acquire up to 70% of the Elk City and Muldoon gold projects in Idaho by funding up to $90M over eight years, with initial budgets totalling $9.4M through 2027.

headline: ONTARIO COMMITS $11M TO MARATHON MINE — C$1.3 BILLION COPPER-PALLADIUM PROJECT NOW FULLY FINANCED FOR CONSTRUCTION
snippet: Ontario's provincial government committed up to $11M to Generation Mining's Marathon copper-palladium project in Northwestern Ontario, stacking on the $140M Canada Growth Fund and $50M Canada Infrastructure Bank commitments. The fully-financed C$1.3B package — which includes a metals streaming deal and commercial lenders — gives Marathon Canada's most de-risked critical minerals construction timeline, with 800 build-phase and 400 permanent jobs on the table.

headline: BANK OF AMERICA HOLDS $130/lb URANIUM TARGET FOR 2027 — CAMECO MINING-TO-DELIVERY GAP FLAGS STRUCTURAL SUPPLY CEILING
snippet: Bank of America reaffirmed its $130/lb uranium target for 2027 — 52% above the current ~$85/lb spot — while noting the "Cameco warning": the world's largest uranium miner plans to produce just 19.5–21.5Mlb this year while delivering 29–32Mlb to customers, drawing down inventories. BofA cut Cameco's price target by 5% on near-term cost pressures but maintained its Buy rating, while Kazatomprom separately confirmed no spot price level would prompt accelerated production.

headline: GDX Q2 2026 FUNDAMENTALS: FREE CASH FLOW MARGIN HITS 24.5% — SECTOR EARNING RECORD CASH WHILE TRADING 20-25% BELOW ALL-TIME HIGHS
snippet: GoldSeek's Q2 2026 gold miners fundamentals analysis finds the VanEck GDX aggregate free cash flow margin at 24.5%, a sixfold rise from 4.2% in Q1 2023, with the broader peer group generating $25.8B in FCF in 2025 alone. With AISC around $1,600/oz against gold at $4,368, miners are pocketing roughly $2,700/oz in margin while the GDX/GDXJ sit 20–25% below their all-time highs — and the group has swung from net debt to net cash.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO'S 12-WEEK ROUND TRIP: 61.7 TO 70.4 BACK TO 66.3 — THREE PHASES AND ONE POSITIONING SETUP
snippet: GoldSilver.com's September ratio analysis tracks the 12-week journey: the gold-silver ratio compressed from 61.7 three months ago, spiked to 70.4 five weeks ago during the rate-hike fear peak, and has now recovered to 66.3 today. The piece identifies three distinct positioning phases — complacency, squeeze, and reversal — and frames 66 as the key decision zone heading into the Sept 24 Trump-Xi summit.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT SUSPENSION EXPIRES NOV 10 — SEPTEMBER BASKET NEAR-FLAT AS TRADERS HOLD BREATH FOR BINARY CATALYST
snippet: The September rare earth basket is essentially flat (average month-over-month change +0.31%), a sharp contrast to August's broad pullback and July's unanimous rally. Every analyst and trader is now focused on a single date: November 10, 2026, when China's rare earth export control suspension expires — the clearest binary catalyst on the calendar, with renewal meaning further supply disruption and expiry signalling a potential normalisation.

headline: THE ASSAYER WEEKLY: EIGHT DEVELOPMENTS AND ONE RATE HIKE — HOW JUNIOR MINING ABSORBED THE FED'S SEPTEMBER MOVE
snippet: The Assayer's post-Fed weekly ledger rounds up eight key mining and commodity developments from the week that included the Fed's 25bp rate hike on September 15-16, examining which juniors and commodities absorbed the shock and which outperformed. A useful map of what moved, what held, and what to watch heading into the high-stakes Trump-Xi summit week beginning September 24.
